General-purpose variant/value container with reference-counted semantics, similar to a JSON Value. Stores primitives as strings internally and aggregates as either an object (map) or array, using WonderTrader collection types. Provides typed accessors, append methods, and factory constructors for all supported ValueType variants. Memory management integrates with WTSObject reference counting; release() frees owned storage when refcount reaches one.

functions.name: ObjectPool::ObjectPool
functions.description: Constructs an ObjectPool that manages fixed-size allocations for T using boost::pool, initializing the internal pool with blocks sized to sizeof(T). Typical usage: create an ObjectPool<T> instance before calling construct/destroy to manage T instances efficiently.
requirements: No arguments required.
The pool is not thread-safe; if accessed from multiple threads, callers must provide external synchronization.
Creating an ObjectPool does not allocate objects; allocation happens in construct().

functions.name: ObjectPool::~ObjectPool
functions.description: Destroys the ObjectPool. It does not automatically destroy any remaining T instances; it only tears down the underlying pool object.
requirements: All objects previously returned by construct() should be destroyed via destroy() before the pool is destroyed, otherwise memory/resources may be leaked.
The pool is not thread-safe; ensure no concurrent access during destruction.

functions.name: ObjectPool::construct
functions.description: Allocates uninitialized storage for a T from the internal boost::pool and default-constructs a T in-place using placement new, returning a pointer to the new object. Returns nullptr if the underlying pool allocation (malloc) fails. Caller should destroy the object with destroy().
requirements: T must be default-constructible and its default constructor must be accessible.
Caller must check for a nullptr return and handle allocation failure.
If T’s constructor throws, the exception will propagate and the allocated pool chunk will not be freed by this function; callers should be prepared for this behavior.
Objects returned must later be passed to destroy() exactly once.
The returned pointer must not be used after being passed to destroy().
Not thread-safe; concurrent calls require external synchronization.

functions.name: ObjectPool::destroy
functions.description: Destroys a T previously created by construct() by explicitly invoking its destructor and returning the memory block to the underlying boost::pool.
requirements: pobj must be a non-null pointer previously returned by this ObjectPool<T>::construct() invocation (same pool instance).
pobj must point to a live T that has not already been destroyed.
Do not pass pointers not allocated by this pool or already freed pointers (no double free).
After destroy(pobj), the pointer becomes invalid and must not be dereferenced.
T’s destructor must be accessible.
Not thread-safe; concurrent calls require external synchronization.

functions.name: ObjectPool::release
functions.description: Manually releases unused memory held by the pool back to the system by calling boost::pool<>::release_memory(). Live objects are unaffected; only currently free blocks may be released.
requirements: Should only be called when it is acceptable to release currently free capacity; objects still allocated remain valid.
Not thread-safe; concurrent calls require external synchronization.
Must not be relied upon to free memory still in use by live objects.

functions.name: wt_strcpy
functions.signature: size_t wt_strcpy(char* des, const char* src, size_t len = 0)
functions.description: Copies a C-string from src to des and appends a null terminator. If len is 0, it computes strlen(src) and copies that many bytes; otherwise it copies exactly len bytes from src (raw bytes, may include embedded NULs) and then writes des[len] = '\0'. Returns the number of bytes copied excluding the terminator. Intended as a lightweight alternative to strcpy/memcpy+terminate; no bounds checking is performed.
requirements: des must be a valid, writable buffer with capacity of at least len+1 bytes (or strlen(src)+1 if len==0).
src must be a valid readable buffer; if len==0, src must be a null-terminated C-string; if len>0, src must provide at least len readable bytes.
Behavior is undefined for overlapping buffers (uses memcpy semantics).
The function always writes one terminating '\0' at des[len]; ensure the destination has room for it.
Return value is the number of bytes copied before the terminator (len or strlen(src)).

functions.name: wt_stricmp
functions.signature: int wt_stricmp(const char* s1, const char* s2)
functions.description: Case-insensitive comparison of two null-terminated C-strings. This name is a macro alias to the platform function (_stricmp on MSVC, strcasecmp on non-MSVC). Returns an integer less than, equal to, or greater than zero if s1 is found to be less than, to match, or be greater than s2 in a case-insensitive lexicographical comparison.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be valid pointers to null-terminated C-strings.
Return value follows strcmp-style conventions: <0 if s1<s2, 0 if equal, >0 if s1>s2 (case-insensitive).
Exact collation details depend on the underlying platform implementation (_stricmp or strcasecmp).

import random
import struct
import itertools

def _rand_ascii(rng, min_len, max_len):
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Mix of printable ASCII and some whitespace, avoid embedded NULs here
    chars = []
    for _ in range(n):
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            chars.append(rng.choice(['\t', '\n', ' ']))
        else:
            chars.append(chr(rng.randint(32, 126)))
    return ''.join(chars).encode('ascii', 'ignore')

def _rand_bytes(rng, min_len, max_len):
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _make_cstring(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure exactly one terminating NUL at end and no other constraints.
    if data.endswith(b"\x00"):
        return data
    return data + b"\x00"

def _interesting_sources(rng):
    # Create a diverse set of candidate source buffers.
    candidates = []

    # 1) Empty C-string
    candidates.append(b"\x00")

    # 2) Small short strings
    for s in [b"", b"A", b"abc", b"hello world", b"CaseSensitive", b"MiXeD123_:-)"]:
        candidates.append(_make_cstring(s))

    # 3) Long ASCII string (~1k) to exercise strlen path and cap switching
    long_ascii = _rand_ascii(rng, 900, 1200)
    candidates.append(_make_cstring(long_ascii))

    # 4) Random binary with embedded NULs; ensure there is at least one NUL not at end
    bin_len = rng.randint(16, 128)
    rb = bytearray(_rand_bytes(rng, bin_len, bin_len))
    if bin_len:
        rb[rng.randrange(bin_len)] = 0
    # For raw len>0 mode, we don't require termination, but FUZZ_PARAM_STR returns a C-string,
    # so ensure termination to be safe; embedded NULs remain inside.
    candidates.append(_make_cstring(bytes(rb)))

    # 5) Repeated patterns
    pattern = (b"\xFF\x00\x01\x7FABcdEF" * rng.randint(5, 50))
    candidates.append(_make_cstring(pattern))

    # 6) Numeric-looking strings (to mimic typical configs)
    for s in [b"0", b"1234567890", b"-42", b"3.14159", b"1e10", b"true", b"yes", b"False"]:
        candidates.append(_make_cstring(s))

    # 7) Whitespace-heavy and edge characters
    ws = b" \t\n" * rng.randint(10, 200)
    candidates.append(_make_cstring(ws))

    # 8) Very large but capped near kMaxCopy to exercise boundary conditions
    near_cap = _rand_ascii(rng, 1000, 1300)
    candidates.append(_make_cstring(near_cap))

    # 9) UTF-8 like content (though FUZZ_PARAM_STR treats as bytes), ensure termination
    utf8_samples = [
        "こんにちは世界".encode("utf-8"),
        "😀😃😄😁😆".encode("utf-8"),
        "áéíóúñç".encode("utf-8"),
    ]
    for b in utf8_samples:
        candidates.append(_make_cstring(b))

    # 10) Strings with internal NUL at start positions
    head_nul = b"\x00" + _rand_ascii(rng, 5, 20)
    candidates.append(_make_cstring(head_nul))

    return candidates


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    candidates = _interesting_sources(rng)
    # Randomly pick one candidate, with a slight bias to larger ones
    weights = []
    for c in candidates:
        # weight proportional to length to bias toward longer cases
        weights.append(max(1, len(c)))
    src = rng.choices(candidates, weights=weights, k=1)[0]

    # FUZZ_PARAM_STR will receive this buffer; ensure it is <= 4096
    if len(src) > 4096:
        src = src[:4096-1] + b"\x00"

    # Return as bytes. The fuzzer will feed this to FUZZ_PARAM_STR so strlen() paths are valid.
    return src

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: null-terminated string consumed by functions expecting C-strings
# Fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR and filenames. We will provide a bytes buffer that
# contains multiple interesting null-terminated strings concatenated, so the harness
# can slice from it. We must keep the data valid (no malformed encodings required),
# but include a variety of contents to exercise behaviors:
# - Empty strings
# - Very short strings
# - Mixed case for wt_stricmp
# - Long strings within caps (<= 1024 for wt_strcpy expectations)
# - Strings with spaces, punctuation, unicode (UTF-8), numbers, booleans (true/yes)
# - Strings with embedded NUL boundaries (separate C-strings)
# - Paths/filenames-like strings
# - Numeric strings to feed WTSVariant conversions (int32/64, uint32/64, double)
# The overall buffer is a series of C-strings separated by NUL, and ends with an extra NUL.

_MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_PUNCT = "!@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{};:'\",.<>/?|`~"
UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "π", "ß", "ø", "漢字", "🙂", "ñ", "é", "Ω", "€", "Русский", "العربية",
]

BOOL_STRINGS = ["true", "false", "True", "FALSE", "yes", "no", "YeS", "NO"]

# Various numeric edge cases as strings
INT32_MIN = str(-(2**31))
INT32_MAX = str(2**31 - 1)
UINT32_MAX = str(2**32 - 1)
INT64_MIN = str(-(2**63))
INT64_MAX = str(2**63 - 1)
UINT64_MAX = str(2**64 - 1)

NUMERIC_STRINGS = [
    "0", "1", "-1", INT32_MIN, INT32_MAX, UINT32_MAX,
    INT64_MIN, INT64_MAX, UINT64_MAX,
    "3.1415926535", "-0.000001", "1e10", "-2.5E-8",
]

PATH_TEMPLATES = [
    "/etc/wondertrader/config.yaml",
    "/etc/wondertrader/config.json",
    "./relative/path/config.yaml",
    "C:/Program Files/WonderTrader/config.yaml",
    "C:/tmp/test.json",
    "../up/dir/file.yaml",
]

WORDS = [
    "alpha", "Beta", "GAMMA", "delta", "epsilon", "Zeta", "eta", "Theta",
    "kappa", "Lambda", "Mu", "Nu", "Xi", "Omicron", "Pi", "Rho",
]


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + ASCII_PUNCT + " "
    return "".join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _case_mix(r: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    out = []
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isalpha() and r.random() < 0.5:
            out.append(ch.upper() if ch.islower() else ch.lower())
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return "".join(out)


def _make_interesting_strings(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    items: List[str] = []

    # Always include some core cases
    items.append("")  # empty string
    items.append("a")
    items.append("A")
    items.append("abc")
    items.append("ABC")
    items.append("AbC")

    # Booleans
    items.extend(BOOL_STRINGS)

    # Numerics
    items.extend(NUMERIC_STRINGS)

    # Unicode samples
    items.extend(UNICODE_SAMPLES)

    # Paths/filenames
    items.extend(PATH_TEMPLATES)

    # Mixed-case words for stricmp
    for w in WORDS:
        items.append(_case_mix(r, w))

    # Long but bounded strings (for wt_strcpy cap 1024). Generate a couple around boundaries.
    long_len_options = [64, 255, 512, 1000]
    for ln in long_len_options:
        items.append(_rand_ascii(r, ln))

    # Random variable strings
    for _ in range(r.randint(5, 12)):
        kind = r.random()
        if kind < 0.25:
            items.append(_rand_ascii(r, r.randint(1, 40)))
        elif kind < 0.5:
            base = r.choice(WORDS)
            items.append(_case_mix(r, base * r.randint(1, 3)))
        elif kind < 0.75:
            items.append(r.choice(NUMERIC_STRINGS))
        else:
            items.append(r.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES) + _rand_ascii(r, r.randint(0, 10)))

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    dedup: List[str] = []
    for s in items:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            dedup.append(s)

    return dedup


def _encode_cstring_chunks(strings: List[str], budget: int) -> bytes:
    # Join as NUL-separated C-strings, ensuring total size <= budget and terminated with an extra NUL
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')  # valid UTF-8 only
        # Each item needs len(b)+1 bytes (including its trailing NUL)
        if len(out) + len(b) + 1 > budget:
            break
        out += b + b"\x00"
    # Ensure at least one terminator and not exceed budget
    if not out or out[-1] != 0:
        if len(out) + 1 <= budget:
            out += b"\x00"
        else:
            # Trim last byte and ensure terminator
            out = out[:-1] + b"\x00"
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a diverse list of strings
    strings = _make_interesting_strings(r)

    # Shuffle a subset to introduce seeded variability
    r.shuffle(strings)

    # Optionally bias-insert pairs useful for comparisons (same string different case)
    if strings:
        pick = r.choice(strings)
        strings.insert(0, pick)
        strings.insert(1, pick.upper())
        strings.insert(2, pick.lower())

    # Ensure presence of keys that may be looked up in object variants commonly
    common_keys = [
        "name", "id", "value", "enabled", "disabled", "version", "items",
        "path", "config", "timeout", "threshold", "rate", "price",
    ]
    # Prepend some deterministic keys
    strings = common_keys + strings

    # Encode into a single byte buffer as NUL-terminated segments
    buf = _encode_cstring_chunks(strings, _MAX_TOTAL)
    return buf
